edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text via First1KGreek; second witness (Lightfoot 1889 / Funk) not yet locked. Chapters 1-9 survive in Greek.

source_text: [1] Καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι δὲ εὔσπλαγχνοι, εἰς πάντας ἐλεήμονες, ἐπιστρέφοντες τὰ ἀποπεπλανημένα, ἐπισκεπτόμενοι πάντας ἀσθενεῖς, μὴ ἀμελοῦντες χήρας ἢ ὀρφανοῦ ἢ πένητος ἀλλὰ προνοοῦντες ἀεὶ τοῦ καλοῦ ἐνώπιον θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων, ἀπεχόμενοι πάσης ὀργῆς, προσωποληψίας, κρίσεως ἀδίκου, μακρὰν ὄντες πάσης φιλαργυρίας, μὴ ταχέως πιστεύοντες κατά τινος, μὴ ἀπότομοι ἐν κρίσει, εἰδότες ὅτι πάντες ὀφειλέται ἐσμὲν ἁμαρτίας. [2] εἰ οὖν δεόμεθα τοῦ κυρίου, ἵνα ἡμῖν ἀφῇ, ὀφείλομεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφιέναι: ἀπέναντι γὰρ τῶν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ θεοῦ ἐσμὲν ὀφθαλμῶν, καὶ πάντας δεῖ παραστῆναι τῷ βήματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἕκαστον ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ λόγον δοῦναι. [3] οὕτως οὖν δουλεύσωμεν αὐτῷ μετὰ φόβου καὶ πάσης εὐλαβείας, καθὼς αὐτὸς ἐνετείλατο καὶ οἱ εὐαγγελισάμενοι ἡμᾶς ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ προφῆται, οἱ προκηρύξαντες τὴν ἔλευσιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν: ζηλωταὶ περὶ τὸ καλόν, ἀπεχόμενοι τῶν σκανδάλων καὶ τῶν ψευδαδέλφων καὶ τῶν ἐν ὑποκρίσει φερόντων τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίον, οἵτινες ἀποπλανῶσι κενοὺς ἀνθρώπους.
thought_title: Presbyters who are merciful, and a people who forgive
pass_a_gloss: And the presbyters too must be compassionate, merciful toward all, turning back those who have strayed, visiting all the sick, not neglecting widow or orphan or poor person, but always taking forethought for what is good before God and men, abstaining from all anger, partiality, unjust judgment, being far from all love of money, not quickly believing something against anyone, not severe in judgment, knowing that we are all debtors of sin. If then we ask the Lord to forgive us, we too ought to forgive; for we are before the eyes of the Lord and God, and all must stand beside the judgment seat of Christ and each give an account for himself. So then let us serve him with fear and all reverence, just as he himself commanded, and the apostles who preached the gospel to us, and the prophets who proclaimed beforehand the coming of our Lord: being zealous about the good, abstaining from stumbling blocks and from false brothers and from those who bear the name of the Lord in hypocrisy, who lead empty men astray.
pass_b_english: The presbyters, for their part, must be tenderhearted and merciful to everyone. They should bring back those who have wandered, visit all who are sick, and never neglect a widow, an orphan, or anyone poor, but always take thought for what is good in the sight of God and people (Proverbs 3:4; 2 Corinthians 8:21). Let them keep clear of all anger, favoritism, and unjust judgment, and stay far from every love of money. They must not be quick to believe an accusation against anyone or harsh in judging, knowing that we are all in debt to sin.

If, then, we ask the Lord to forgive us, we too must forgive (Matthew 6:12, 14), for we are before the eyes of the Lord and God, and all of us must stand before the judgment seat of Christ, and each must give an account of himself (Romans 14:10, 12).

So let us serve him with fear and all reverence (Hebrews 12:28), just as he himself commanded, and the apostles who brought us the gospel, and the prophets who foretold our Lord's coming. Let us be zealous for what is good, and keep away from stumbling blocks, from false brothers, and from those who bear the name of the Lord in hypocrisy, who lead empty people astray.

choices.why: keeps the debt image that sets up 'forgive' (Matt 6:12)

choices.english: carry the Lord's name as a mask
choices.why: ὑπόκρισις is stage-acting; 'mask' keeps the image

choices.english: as the apostles… and the prophets… have taught
choices.why: the Greek lists them as co-subjects of the command; 'have taught' makes the elliptical clause clear without adding a claim

review.notes: Paragraph [1] only. Greek 'Καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι δὲ εὔσπλαγχνοι... μὴ ταχέως πιστεύοντες κατά τινος, μὴ ἀπότομοι ἐν κρίσει, εἰδότες ὅτι πάντες ὀφειλέται ἐσμὲν ἁμαρτίας' matches A 'not quickly believing something against anyone, not severe in judgment, knowing that we are all debtors of sin' and B 'must not be quick to believe an accusation against anyone or harsh in judging, knowing that we are all in debt to sin.' Reciprocity, γάρ, and the tribunal are kept: 'ὀφείλομεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφιέναι: ἀπέναντι γὰρ τῶν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ θεοῦ ἐσμὲν ὀφθαλμῶν... λόγον δοῦναι' / A 'we too ought to forgive; for we are before the eyes of the Lord and God... each give an account for himself.' The καθὼς list adds no verb: 'καθὼς αὐτὸς ἐνετείλατο καὶ οἱ εὐαγγελισάμενοι ἡμᾶς ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ προφῆται' / A 'just as he himself commanded, and the apostles who preached the gospel to us, and the prophets who proclaimed beforehand the coming of our Lord.' Hypocrisy stays literal: 'τῶν ἐν ὑποκρίσει φερόντων τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίον, οἵτινες ἀποπλανῶσι κενοὺς ἀνθρώπους' / 'those who bear the name of the Lord in hypocrisy, who lead empty men astray.' Negations, first-person 'we,' and hortatory δουλεύσωμεν are intact. Title names the thought. Inline verse tags are identifications beside the alluded clauses, not a fidelity fail.

Paragraph 1 fully corresponds. Greek source: 'Καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι δὲ εὔσπλαγχνοι... ἀποπλανῶσι κενοὺς ἀνθρώπους.' matches Pass A's comprehensive rendering and Pass B's three-part subdivision. All clauses present, including 'μὴ ταχέως πιστεύοντες κατά τινος' (not quickly believing something against anyone) reflected in both Pass A and Pass B. Negation preserved (μὴ ἀμελοῦντες, μὴ ταχέως πιστεύοντες, etc.), agency clear (presbyters act, 'we' forgive, 'we' serve), modality correct (ought, must, let us), doctrine intact (debtors of sin, judgment before Christ). Scripture citations accurately aligned: Proverbs 3:4; 2 Cor 8:21 with προνοοῦντes... ἐνώπιον θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων; Matt 6:12,14 with ἀφῇ... ἀφιέναι; Rom 14:10,12 with παραστῆναι τῷ βήματι... λόγον δοῦνai; Heb 12:28 with μετὰ... εὐλαβείας. Title names the thought (mercy and forgiveness as communal virtues). Notes disclose OCR/re-attribution and variants. No omissions, contradictions, or false additions.
